decision: candidate improves observed empty-tunnel nuisance load, subject to the explicit untested long-object and causal-runtime risks below; this is not a field-safety certification
hypothesis: A point is attributed to the tunnel only if its narrow rail-relative lateral AND height cell is occupied at at least three distinct longitudinal stations spanning at least 5 m, in addition to the existing outward-reach structural criterion. A coarse cell alone is insufficient.

comparison.input_identity: All 13558 negative frames matched by frame, measurement timestamp and source scan ID; geometry point count and supported range identical. All 11271 extended poses and all 2287 negative original poses matched under numpy allclose atol=1e-7, rtol=1e-5; native binary and bag metadata hashes match. See run-local manifests for every source, input and binary digest.
comparison.source_difference: Before extended and six-recording replays predate the uncommitted route-memory and PointCloud2 input changes. These source/config differences prevent an identical-source causal timing claim. The route-memory observer is diagnostic; the candidate extended run did accept one map bridge at an acquisition gap, but neither that map nor its candidate positions enter cluster classification. No pose or supported-range difference exceeded the specified comparison.
comparison.episode_rule: Within each recording, join obstacle frames with consecutive confirmed measurement timestamps no more than 0.5 s apart; any acquisition gap greater than 0.5 s cuts an episode, even across track-ID changes. Do not join different recordings. Duration uses first-to-last measurement timestamp, not repeated frames as independent objects.
comparison.occupancy_rule: Each frame receives the elapsed time until the next frame when that interval is in (0, 0.5] seconds; otherwise use 0.1 seconds as the nominal frame exposure. This excludes unobserved acquisition gaps from alarm-on time. The final frame receives 0.1 s. All exposure figures are approximate due to cadence and gaps.

negative_panel.label_provenance: Organizer statement reported in #21: five original tunnels and the 20-minute extended recording are empty; not independently exhaustive annotation of every surface. Already inspected: evaluation is not blind.

person_episode.label: annotations/doubleT-obstacle-person.json
person_episode.interpretation: The 82 removed obstacle frames cannot be attributed to the adjacent person. Nor can this nonexhaustive person annotation certify that no other on-track object was affected.

hybrid_synthetic_central.limitations: HYBRID SYNTHETIC from two recorded scans; 28 misses in both versions. Not a field recall estimate and does not cover long objects.

hybrid_synthetic_edge.reason: Generator labels hazards only for |lateral| < rail_gauge/2; all selected edge positions were >=0.9 m, so it emitted zero annotated positives even though objects had visible returns. Its null recall cannot be called a pass.
hybrid_synthetic_edge.paired_manual_support_result: Every visible inserted support that intersected an output box retained the same adjacent/intersecting/confirmed outcome in both variants; this is an overlap audit, not calibrated hazard recall.

examples.cause: Two compact components near 54 and 56 m had two core points each, same narrow lateral/height cells occupied over 20-22 m; last rail anchor at 35 m. Structural returns plus extrapolated corridor, not a proven independent obstacle.
Two 2-3-core-point components at 56-59 m with narrow cell support spanning 58-70 m; last rail anchor at 39.65 m. Geometry continuation and infrastructure overlap.

A near 2-5.6 m infrastructure component with 471 points, 265 nominal certified points and all in cells shared with structure; its narrow cells persist along the tunnel. This is structural support, not evidence from the reason string alone.

Merged walkway/wall component extends 16.87 m forward and 3.15 m high; its core lies on the longitudinal structure. Last rail anchor at 7.81 m, so corridor continuation also contributes. Other simultaneously alarmed components remain unresolved in attribution.

cost_and_risks.why: Original six control/candidate and development replays had opposite per-recording timing shifts under varying machine load. A direct ten-repeat call of the new fine mask on 40,600 measured points averaged 7.8 ms; this is an isolated local measurement, not full-detector speed. ROS2 and target Intel were not timed.
cost_and_risks.risk: A long or infrastructure-attached real object can share both fine longitudinal support and outward reach with a tunnel surface, and a weak object can fail candidate admission once its interior points are attributed to that surface. The real person is adjacent, not an on-track safety positive. Cannot claim measured recall on actual on-track hazards, independent precision, or 10 Hz.
cost_and_risks.prior_rejected_shortcut: results/empty-tunnel-alarm-load-attempt2-20260919.json documents the failed coarse-cell and status-demotion approaches. They cannot be repackaged as successful fixes.
cost_and_risks.unrun_challenge: No elongated, infrastructure-attached object challenge was run; no safety claim follows from it.

verification: Actual detector CLI on six complete original recordings and one complete extended recording; measured-support diagnostics from the real CLI; paired HYBRID SYNTHETIC CLI; no automated tests created or run.
